Mounting Your Phone Safely on a Motorcycle

Your smartphone is a powerful navigation tool, music player, and communication device. But mounting it on a motorcycle requires careful consideration. Vibration from the engine and road surface can damage your phone's camera stabilisation system, and an insecure mount risks losing an expensive device at speed.

The Vibration Problem

Apple and other manufacturers have confirmed that motorcycle vibrations can damage the optical image stabilisation and autofocus systems in phone cameras. High-frequency vibrations from certain engines are particularly damaging. To protect your phone, always use a vibration-dampened mount rather than a rigid one that transmits vibrations directly.

Mount Types

  • Quad Lock — The most popular system using a case with a twist-lock mechanism. The vibration dampener accessory is essential for motorcycle use. Quick to attach and detach with one hand.
  • RAM Mount — The versatile choice with a ball-and-socket system and X-Grip holder. Works with any phone in any case. The rubber arms grip securely and the articulating arm positions the phone precisely.
  • SP Connect — A slim mounting system with a strong twist-lock. The anti-vibration module protects the phone and the mount profile is lower than most alternatives.
  • Peak Design — Magnetic mounting with a secondary locking mechanism. Slim case design and quick release. The motorcycle bar mount includes vibration dampening.

Waterproofing

Modern phones have IP68 water resistance, but this does not account for sustained rain exposure at motorway speeds. Consider a waterproof phone case or mount cover for touring in wet conditions. Some mounts like Quad Lock offer an optional rain cover that seals the phone while allowing touchscreen use through the cover.

Best Phone Mounts for Touring

Quad Lock Motorcycle Kit with Dampener — The complete solution. Case, mount, and vibration dampener in one package. Available for all major phone models. The dampener genuinely reduces harmful vibrations.

RAM X-Grip with Anti-Vibe Base — Universal holder working with any phone. The anti-vibration base isolates the phone from engine and road vibrations effectively.

SP Connect Moto Bundle — Slim and secure with good vibration dampening. The case adds minimal bulk to your phone for daily off-bike use.

If you rely on your phone camera for photography during tours, seriously consider a dedicated GPS instead of mounting your phone. No mount can completely eliminate vibration risk, and camera damage is not covered by most warranties.

Positioning Your Phone

Mount the phone where a quick glance gives you navigation info without moving your head from the forward riding position. Above the instrument cluster or to one side of the handlebars works best. Avoid mounting directly in your primary line of sight which creates a distraction.

faq.q: Can a motorcycle really damage my phone camera?
faq.a: Yes. Apple and other manufacturers have confirmed that high-frequency motorcycle vibrations can damage the optical image stabilisation and autofocus systems in phone cameras. Certain engines are worse than others. Always use a vibration-dampened mount rather than a rigid one, and if you depend on your phone for photography, consider a dedicated GPS for navigation instead.

faq.q: Which phone mount is best for motorcycles?
faq.a: Quad Lock is the most popular, using a case with a twist-lock mechanism and an essential vibration dampener accessory for bikes. RAM Mount is the most versatile, working with any phone in any case via its X-Grip and Anti-Vibe base. SP Connect is slim and secure, and Peak Design offers magnetic mounting with a secondary lock. All are strong choices with the right anti-vibration part fitted.

faq.q: Are phones waterproof enough for motorcycle use?
faq.a: Most modern phones have IP68 water resistance, but this is tested in still water, not sustained rain at 70mph. Driving rain can eventually work its way in. For wet-weather touring, use a waterproof phone case or a mount rain cover. Quad Lock offers a rain cover that seals the phone while still allowing touchscreen use through the cover.

faq.q: Where should I position the phone on the bike?
faq.a: Mount the phone where a quick glance gives you navigation information without moving your head from the forward riding position, typically above the instrument cluster or to one side of the handlebars. Avoid mounting it directly in your primary line of sight, as that becomes a distraction and can block your view of the road ahead.

faq.q: Do I really need the anti-vibration accessory?
faq.a: For a motorcycle, yes. The base mount alone transmits engine and road vibration straight into your phone. The dedicated anti-vibration module or base isolates the phone and significantly reduces the frequencies most likely to harm the camera. It is an inexpensive addition that protects a device worth many times its cost.
